newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended firmer on Wednesday, except shorter term paper which suffered from continued talk about possible rate rises, traders said.
On Tuesday, short paper dipped as the guilder fell against the mark and prompted speculation that the Dutch central bank would be forced to raise rates on Thursday.

On Wednesday, the guilder's recovery led many in the market to dismiss the possibility of an isolated Dutch rate hike. But Dutch bonds mirrored the flattening of the bund market in which there were renewed suspicions that the Bundesbank might intervene to support the mark against the dollar.
"It doesn't look like we'll get a (Dutch) rate rise tomorrow... the short end has really just followed Germany down," one trader said.
The guilder picked up from 1.1269 German marks at yesterday's close to 1.1263 today.
"When the guilder has this strength, there doesn't seem to be a reason to raise rates," one dealer said.
Nevertheless the market will still keenly follow the Dutch central bank's announcement on Thursday afternoon concerning the next special advances pact.
While most questioned in the market said they foresaw no rate rise, some said the bank could opt for a shorter pact, giving it greater flexibility to intervene should the guilder again suffer.
